Natural-language security analytics

2023 – present

Analysts ask questions in plain English. The system picks the capabilities the question needs, runs them concurrently across internal security data and five threat-intelligence services, and returns a grounded answer with its queries and raw rows exposed.

PythonLangGraph PostgreSQLOpenSearch self-hosted LLM
  • Deploys against a different organization's data with no code change — 40 tables and ~1,700 fields resolved at runtime from catalogs, enforced by an automated audit.
  • Concurrent plan → execute → synthesize → review orchestration, so multi-source questions cost the slower path rather than the sum.
  • Self-describing capability registry — adding a capability is one registration instead of three files kept manually in sync.
  • Worst-case query 232s → 66s, with 62 automated tests written from zero.

EvalForge — LLM evaluation platform

Live

A platform for measuring whether a RAG system is actually any good. Teams plug in their documents and a benchmark question set; it scores answers on retrieval quality, faithfulness and hallucination, then tracks how those scores move as prompts and models change.

FastAPIPostgreSQL QdrantLangChain RAGASDeepEval DockerGCP
Open the app → Browse the API →
  • 18 metrics per answer across three families — classical NLP, retrieval quality (Recall@K, MRR, NDCG), and LLM-as-judge faithfulness scoring.
  • Statement-level hallucination analysis that isolates which specific claims the retrieved context does not support.
  • Its own regression harness caught a change of mine that quietly degraded quality — reverted and reimplemented before it shipped.
  • Provisioned and operates the full deployment: containerized services, managed relational and vector stores, auto-renewing HTTPS.

Agentic research assistant

Live

Give it a research topic. It searches arXiv, embeds what it finds, retrieves the passages that bear on your question, and answers from those with citations back to the papers.

  • Two retrieval bugs worth the trouble: arXiv treats an unquoted phrase as loose terms, so "retrieval augmented generation" returned papers on wearables until I quoted it.
  • And embedding the question alone left similarity near 0.08 — a generic question carries no topical signal. Retrieving on topic + question lifted it to 0.40.
  • Refuses to answer when the retrieved text doesn't support one, rather than filling the gap.

Cascade learning on Spark

Results

A cheap model answers what it is confident about; only the residual escalates to an expensive one. Run over 581,012 rows with Spark MLlib.

  • Retains 99.1% of a random forest's accuracy while avoiding 44% of its work.
  • Swept across nine confidence thresholds — the useful region is the knee, and picking a point on it is a product decision about what a millisecond costs.

Movie recommender

Live

Item-item collaborative filtering over the MovieLens ratings matrix — no genre matching, only what people actually watched together.

Recipe recommender

Live

Content-based similarity over recipes. The real work is parsing — 2/3 cup panko has to become panko, or every recipe looks alike because they all contain cups and teaspoons.

  • 96% tag agreement@5 against a 38.5% random baseline — a 2.49× lift.
  • Content-based by necessity: the corpus carries no user ratings, so claiming a hybrid model would be fiction — and it handles a brand-new recipe with zero history.

How I work

The dangerous failure isn't a crash — it's a confident wrong answer.

Three things I've learned building systems where the output looks right either way.

01

Assume the model is lying until the data says otherwise

A search filter looked correct and returned zero results, because an identifier meant something different in each data source it was applied to. The answer read perfectly. It matched nothing.

Constrain generation per source, then validate in code.
02

Budget the resource that actually runs out

A pipeline kept hitting the context limit despite a row cap that looked conservative. The cap counted rows; the cost is in tokens — and row width varied ~100× between tables, so a "safe" limit exceeded the entire window.

Measure the real budget at runtime, allocate by share.
03

Prompt instructions are not enforcement

Repeatedly, the prompt already forbade the exact behaviour a model then produced. Where correctness matters, the prompt states intent and code guarantees it — with every automated rewrite logged so a wrong answer can be traced.

Verified by a fixed benchmark diffed on every change.
